Resolves #19220

`Main#windowOpen` makes a popup's requested height its total height — the window takes the size of the widget it replaces, the content a little smaller. It built that resize from the newborn's own `outerWidth` and `innerHeight`. An unemulated Chrome answers `outerWidth 0` for a popup that has no frame yet (measured: `innerWidth 320, innerHeight 239, outerWidth 0, outerHeight 0` synchronously after `window.open`), so `resizeTo(0, 239)` landed on the platform's minimum width: the film's capture mode birthed every vessel at 146×239 while the emulated tour, whose metrics answer the request at once, saw 320×240. The resize now takes its numbers from the feature string (`Main.parseWindowFeatureSize`, `width`/`height` or their `inner*` spellings); a request that names no size is left as the platform made it. Same intent, same outcome under emulation, and a real window now matches it.

Evidence: L3 achieved (one headed capture-mode run on the film-stage display: both vessels 320×240 outer / 320×173 inner from first paint) → L3 required (AC-2). Residual: none for this ticket; the compose beat's remaining capture-mode cause is the follow origin, its own ticket (see #19220's Related).

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the CI baseline jobs ran.

| AC-3 | Tracked film arm under emulation, headless, three runs at this head: the only error is `film-reintegration[0] … native frame movement was refused`, the native-return beat headless refuses by construction; every beat before it, the compose beat included, passed. |
| AC-4 | `test/playwright/unit/main/MainWindowOpen.spec.mjs`: a frameless newborn (`outerWidth 0`) is resized to `[320, 240]`; a readable frame gets the same; a request naming no size gets no resize. On `dev`: two of three red (`resizeTo(0, 239)` in both cases); with the fix 3/3. |

## Deltas from ticket
The ticket's original AC-2 also asked for the compose beat to settle. With the size fixed the beat still reports `target vessel did not reach one parked semantic + rendered claim`: the target claims the pointer (`claimCount 1`) and the conversion never proposes, because the born vessel's content sits one title bar below where the pointer-follow places its outer origin, so the inner rects overlap too little on the y axis for the 0.55 threshold. That is a different owner (the follow origin), so the ticket was restated to the size and the beat moved to its own ticket.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19220 as restated (the layer, the fix, AC-1…AC-4); the changed-file list (`src/Main.mjs`, a new `test/playwright/unit/main/MainWindowOpen.spec.mjs`); `dev`'s `Main#windowOpen` (the `useTotalHeight` branch `resizeTo(openedWindow.outerWidth, openedWindow.innerHeight)`); the resize's origin, f91e513809 (#8121, "enforcing a 'fixed' popup size", the popup sized to the dragged proxy).
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Take the total size from the request, i.e. the feature string the caller already built, not from the newborn's unlaid metrics. No title-bar or emulation constants. Leave a window whose request names no size as the platform made it. Test isolation: a frameless-newborn arm (outer 0), a readable-frame parity control, and a no-size arm, each isolated from the shared main-thread globals.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `Main.parseWindowFeatureSize` reads `width`/`height` (or `inner*`), requires both finite and positive, and otherwise returns `null`, so `size && openedWindow.resizeTo(size.width, size.height)` never resizes to a guess. No constants. Each arm runs in its own child `node` process, so the cross-file stub-leak class of #19217 cannot reach it. I confirmed the arms discriminate: at the head 3/3 pass; with `dev`'s `src/Main.mjs` swapped in, 2 fail (frameless newborn, no size) and 1 passes (the readable-frame arm, which is the parity control).

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: The width semantics changed on bordered platforms, and nobody has measured it there.
  - Before, the outer width was the laid-out one: the request plus any side borders the platform draws.
  - Now the outer width is the request, so on a platform with window side borders (Windows, many Linux WMs) the content narrows by the border.
  - This is the #8121 intent (the window takes the size of the widget it replaces), so I don't read it as a regression. But the only receipts are macOS (the film stage) and emulation. A one-run check on a bordered seat belongs with the Post-Merge Validation row if such a seat exists; see the Engine's Seat Evidence Capabilities guide.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**
